segments.title: Staff Report on Waterworks Fund Reallocation
segments.takeaway: Administration presented a report requesting to reallocate $4 million within the waterworks program to integrate treatment process enhancements into the new water treatment plant project.

segments.title: Questions on Waterworks Fund Reallocation
segments.takeaway: Committee members asked administration about the current capacity to handle hydrocarbon spills, the timeline for new plant features, and the upstream water monitoring program.

segments.title: Vote on Waterworks Fund Reallocation

speakers.name: Izabeth Rossi
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Noise Bylaw Extension
said: Outskirts Music Festival requests 1 AM extension on June 27th.
Rock the River requests 11 PM extension from August 13-16.
Proactive sound monitoring and resident engagement minimize event impacts.

speakers.name: Greg Clark
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Hudsons Block Party Noise Bylaw Extension Request
said: Requests noise bylaw extensions for five-day Hudson's Block Party.
New smaller footprint for weekdays minimizes sound bleed.
Sound monitoring and good neighbor relations ensure minimal impact.

segments.title: Staff Report on Noise Bylaw Extension Requests
segments.takeaway: Administration presented requests for noise bylaw extensions for four special events in 2026 that require committee approval due to not meeting delegated criteria.

segments.title: Public Hearing - SAS Health Center Presentation
segments.takeaway: A representative from SAS Health Center presented on the Outskirts Music Festival and Rock the River, detailing their noise management plans and community engagement efforts.

segments.title: Public Hearing - Hudson's Block Party Presentation
segments.takeaway: The operating partner for Hudson's Block Party clarified requested extension times, discussed event growth, and outlined new sound management strategies for the smaller footprint.

segments.title: Questions for Administration on Noise Monitoring
segments.takeaway: Committee members questioned administration about the city's role in monitoring sound levels, the complaint process, and the accuracy of event organizers' reports.

segments.title: Motion to Review Noise Bylaw Guidelines
segments.takeaway: Councillor McDonald moved a motion, later amended by Councillor Timone, for administration to review noise bylaw extension guidelines for standardized decibel level checks.

segments.title: Vote on Original Noise Bylaw Extension Recommendations
segments.takeaway: The committee voted on and passed the original recommendations to approve the noise bylaw extension requests for the four special events.

segments.title: Vote on Noise Bylaw Guidelines Review Motion
segments.takeaway: The committee voted on and carried Councillor McDonald's amended motion for administration to review noise bylaw extension guidelines for standardized decibel level checks.

description: Saskatoon launched an Indigenous apprenticeship program in Fleet Services.
It provides four-year heavy duty mechanic training for two apprentices.
Jointly funded with Saskatoon Tribal Council, it aims for culturally safe employment.

chips.text: Councillor Keller asked about scaling up the program to other trades and departments.
Fleet Services faced vacant heavy duty mechanic positions for over a year.
This is the city's first Indigenous apprenticeship program.
Saskatoon Tribal Council director praised the city's partnership and communication.
Administration committed to exploring scaling the program to other departments and trades.
